whatItIs.text: Paprika (dried, ground red peppers) smoked before milling — Spain's signature version, all bonfire and no burn.

historyNote.text: Capsicum peppers descend from wild ancestors around the Amazon, gathered in Mexico by 7000 BC, and reached Europe in the 16th century; Hungary knew them by 1569, and central European paprika stayed hot until the 1920s, when a Szeged breeder found a sweet-fruited plant.

howToChoose.text: Choose tins labelled pimentón or smoked paprika with a deep red colour and a true smoke smell; sweet (dulce) for general use, hot (picante) if you want the edge.

storage.text: Keep sealed away from light and heat, and replace yearly — old paprika tastes of dust. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: spice storage guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Bloom it in oil or butter for 30 seconds to wake it, then add roasted potatoes, eggs, beans, or mayo; it colours and flavours whatever it touches.

substitutions.substitute: sweet paprika + a drop of liquid smoke
